Where it began

Mark Wood was born in Ashington, Northumberland, on 11 January 1990. His county cricket began close to home, with Northumberland. His first game for them came in 2008, a Knockout Trophy match against Norfolk, and he played Minor Counties cricket for them until 2010.

Durham gave him his first-class debut in 2011, against Durham MCCU, and he made his List A debut the same season. In 2014 he toured Sri Lanka with the England Lions.

The player

He made his Test debut against New Zealand in May 2015, and England won the match by 124 runs. Later that summer, in the fourth Ashes Test, he took the wicket that won the game and with it brought the Ashes back to England. He played 38 Tests between 2015 and 2025, taking 119 wickets at 30.80 with a best of 6 for 37 and five five-wicket hauls. He also made 811 runs, with one fifty and a top score of 52, and held 8 catches.

His first Test five-for came at St Lucia in 2019, 5 for 41 in 8.2 overs, and he was the fastest bowler in the match. In South Africa the following winter he took nine wickets in a Test, and in the third Test of the 2023 Ashes he was man of the match with seven wickets and 40 runs from 16 balls. He was in the England sides that won the 50-over World Cup in 2019 and the T20 World Cup in 2022, one of only six men to be part of both.

What made him special

Pace, first and foremost. From 2020 his average speed in Tests was 89 mph, and he was the quickest bowler at the 2022 T20 World Cup.

His batting was more cheerful than careful. Forty from 16 balls tells you most of what you need to know, and his single Test fifty suggests he was in no hurry to stay out there long enough for a second. A knee injury eventually cut his England career short, and he retired from international cricket in September 2026.

Away from the middle

Wisden named him one of its Cricketers of the Year. Beyond England duty he played in the IPL for Chennai Super Kings and was signed by Lucknow Super Giants, turned out for Durham, and was picked up by the London Spirit for The Hundred in 2022. He supports AFC Wimbledon, a long way from Ashington.

And finally

In the 2019 World Cup final, batting at number 11, he was run out off the very last ball. It tied the match and sent it to a Super Over, which England went on to win. Few run-outs can have ended so happily for the man walking off.
